title: A Lamp's Shadow: The Hyperbola Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Stand a lamp with an open shade close to a wall and the light is not a circle: its edges are two curves, one bending up and one bending down, and they never close. The wall slices the cone of light, and the curve is the hyperbola. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 10, Conic Sections) we find its rule.

You will watch a live point run along both branches while its distances to the two foci grow, yet always differ by 6. We name the vertices, foci and the transverse and conjugate axes, show why c² = a² + b², derive x²/a² - y²/b² = 1 step by step, and grow the eccentricity live to see why it is always more than 1. A side-by-side of the ellipse and the hyperbola with a pause-and-think question, a worked example with 9y² - 16x² = 144, the exam trap about which number is a², an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.

In this video:
0:00 A lamp near a wall: two open curves
0:27 The NCERT definition: a fixed difference
0:39 Live: P runs along both branches
1:06 Vertices, foci, axes and c² = a² + b²
1:49 Deriving x²/a² - y²/b² = 1
2:21 Live: eccentricity e = c/a > 1
2:33 Ellipse vs hyperbola side by side
3:08 Worked example: 9y² - 16x² = 144
3:52 Exam trap: a² sits under the plus term
4:21 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:02 Recap and three questions to answer
